bar.note: iA publishes no latency numbers (only 'boots in a whizz… snappy as jazz'). Bar = best native editors: Sublime 32.5 ms / TextEdit 33.4 ms keyboard-to-photon (Tristan Hume, macOS); internal input→paint ≤5 ms (Typometer, Notepad++ 4.3 ms). Sources in dev/ref/ia/REFERENCE.md.

pieces.title: The page
pieces.judge: the page itself: paper colour, margins, the measure (line length), vertical placement of text in the window, scrolling feel implied by spacing, how the empty space frames the text; overall calm. What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap. The air above and below a heading is not this Piece's row either: docs/design.md row Block spacing, measured off the Design oracle, costs a blank line one pitch and gives a heading no margin of its own, which is what Quill draws — so the space around a heading is a decision already taken and not a gap. Where the page opens is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Page top rests the editor's own page top on a constant 30 logical px, measured off the Design oracle — the 164 device px its first line box stands below the window's top edge, less the 104 px its title bar takes — where the Parity oracle opens two pitches down, 72 px at the default step. So a side whose first line sits higher up the window is a decision already taken and not a gap. pieces.title: Markup rendering
pieces.what: Headings, emphasis, lists, quotes, code, links in the editor
pieces.judge: how Markdown is shown while writing: heading markers, emphasis, lists, blockquotes, code, links — are markers quiet, does the text stay readable, do headings and structure read at a glance without the text jumping. All three states are the hanging-marker gutter and the body column: gutters is the six heading levels, whose `#` runs step out into the left gutter by level + 1 cells so their words all land on the body column and `###### ` reaches the container's own left edge; blocks is that deepest heading above a quote, a bullet and an ordinal, whose markers stand on the body column instead and push their own words inward, with no rule beside the quote; wrapped is a bullet, a three-digit ordinal and a quote each long enough to wrap, so the rows under the first are what there is to read. Judge where each row starts and how the columns read together. What a wrapped item's rows do is docs/design.md row What hangs, measured off the Design oracle: an item's continuation rows hang in under its own first word, by that item's own marker run — two cells for `- ` and `> `, five for `123. ` — and a wrapped quote carries no second `>`, so a continuation that returns to the body column is a fault and one that repeats the marker is another. What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap. Where the page opens is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Page top rests the editor's own page top on a constant 30 logical px, measured off the Design oracle — the 164 device px its first line box stands below the window's top edge, less the 104 px its title bar takes — where the Parity oracle opens two pitches down, 72 px at the default step. So a side whose first line sits higher up the window is a decision already taken and not a gap

pieces.title: Chrome & menus
pieces.what: Bars, counters, palette, what hides while typing, the empty state
pieces.judge: the chrome: what UI is visible around the text, the stats/word-count bar, title, menus/palette, how it recedes while writing; is there exactly as much interface as a writer needs and no more. At bars and empty the comparison is the two bars themselves: a 32 px title bar with a Library toggle at its left, the Document's name centred and a View button at its right, a 26 px stats bar reading words, characters and reading time with the number a weight above the word for it, the hairline rule that stands between a bar and a page continuing past it, and the type size and the title bar's grey the two are set in. What the Characters cell counts is a counting rule and not a gap: ours counts the prose stream, the words as they were written with the Markdown markers and the blank lines between blocks dropped, where the Parity oracle counts the raw characters of the file. So at bars ours reads 929 characters where the oracle reads 961, 32 fewer for the sample's seventeen bytes of marker and its fifteen newlines, while the words and the reading time are the same number on both sides. One cell lower by that much, and only that cell, is the rule this spec landed and a decision already taken. The title reads the Document's file name without its extension (sample for a shot of dev/ref/sample.md, Untitled until the first save), which is what the bar is for and not a gap. The bars' type is set in Adwaita Sans, the GNOME UI face and the counterpart of the SF Pro Text the Design oracle sets its chrome in; the Parity oracle's frozen shots fell through the same font stack to Liberation Sans on the machine that froze them, so a run of chrome text that is a few pixels wider or narrower on one side is the two faces and not a gap — the size and the weight step between a number and its label are what to compare. What an empty Document holds is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Empty document rests an empty page on the caret and the paper alone, measured off the Design oracle — dev/ref/ia/mac-native/NOTES.md § State 3 reads the bar and, under "anything else drawn", nothing — where the Parity oracle whispers "Start writing…" on the first line in its dim grey (page.css). So a placeholder on the Parity side and none on ours is a decision already taken and not a gap. At typing the chrome has stepped back — title bar gone, stats bar dimmed to about a third — and the page under it is unchanged. At palette the Palette is open over the page from Ctrl+K: a panel a third of the way down the window with a search field, a hairline, section headings in small capitals and 24 px rows with the chord at the right, the first row selected in the accent; the comparison is the panel's proportions, its type sizes, its greys and its selected row, not the wording or the number of its rows, which are the registry's (docs/shortcuts.md) and carry every Command the port will have, a row not built yet greyed. At stats-menu the Stats menu is open where a click on the stats bar opens it: six Statistics as checks — Words, Characters, Characters Without Spaces, Sentences, Paragraphs, Reading Time — with Words, Characters and Reading Time ticked, then a separator and Hide Statistics under it. The comparison is the menu's typography, its spacing, its ticks and how it sits over the bar it came from, not its row count or its wording, which are the registry's. At selection a run of the passage is held: the stats bar leads with the word Selection in the accent and the cells after it count the held run rather than the whole Document, at full strength rather than dimmed. The comparison is that label's colour and weight against the numbers beside it, and the row's spacing; whether those numbers actually followed the selection is asserted from typed keys (tools/gate keys chrome) rather than read off this still. The colour of the selection's own fill on the page is docs/design.md row Active fill, measured off the Design oracle, so a fill differing from the oracle there is a decision already taken and not a gap. What the counts are set in is not this Piece's gap: the foot of the window is the Design oracle's, dev/ref/ia/mac-native/NOTES.md § State 27, measured on the Mac and taken there as this spec's decision. It rests the counts at the body's own ink — #191919 on light and #cccccc on dark, an empty Document's 0 included — lifts them to the accent under the pointer, and puts the selection fill behind a held run's figure, where the Parity oracle sets a figure in one grey and its label in a lighter one and marks a held run with the label alone. So a bar whose counts read as dark as the prose, a bar that dims to one ink rather than two while the keys move, and a figure standing on a pale blue fill while a selection is held are decisions already taken and not gaps. One ink for a figure and the word for it is that same decision: the Design oracle sets no grey step between the two, so a figure told from its name by its weight alone, and a row that reads at one ink at a glance, are the foot this spec landed rather than a count that has lost its emphasis. The room, the order and the spacing of the row are what remain to compare. What stands between the last row of the page and the stats bar is not this Piece's gap either: the foot is the Design oracle's, dev/ref/ia/mac-native/NOTES.md § State 27, and it leaves no gutter at all — the last row's ink ends one device pixel above the rule, and the page runs to the rule and scrolls under it — where the Parity oracle leaves a band of paper above its bar. So a side whose text runs closer to the rule at the foot is a decision already taken and not a gap. Nor is the air at the end of a draft: docs/design.md row Page bottom, measured off that same capture, leaves 48.5 % of the view below the last row where the Parity oracle leaves 30 %, so a side whose last row sits higher up a window scrolled to its end is that row and not a gap. What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap. The air above and below a heading is not this Piece's row either: docs/design.md row Block spacing, measured off the Design oracle, costs a blank line one pitch and gives a heading no margin of its own, which is what Quill draws — so the space around a heading is a decision already taken and not a gap. Where the page opens is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Page top rests the editor's own page top on a constant 30 logical px, measured off the Design oracle — the 164 device px its first line box stands below the window's top edge, less the 104 px its title bar takes — where the Parity oracle opens two pitches down, 72 px at the default step. So a side whose first line sits higher up the window is a decision already taken and not a gap. The caret's ends are not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Caret ends, measured off the Design oracle, caps the bar with semicircles of radius half its width, which is what Quill draws, where the Parity oracle's bar is square (caret.css sets no border-radius). So a side whose caret has rounded ends is a decision already taken and not a gap

pieces.title: File handling
pieces.judge: file handling UI: the library/sidebar, file list, how documents are named and found, open/save affordances, how it looks next to the editor; would a writer trust it with their manuscripts. What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap. The air above and below a heading is not this Piece's row either: docs/design.md row Block spacing, measured off the Design oracle, costs a blank line one pitch and gives a heading no margin of its own, which is what Quill draws — so the space around a heading is a decision already taken and not a gap At library and search the comparison is the Library pane alone, cut from both windows — device columns 0 to 719 from the window's top to its bottom, iA Writer for Mac as measured (dev/ref/ia/mac-native/NOTES.md § State 28) on one side: two columns on their own grounds, the Organizer darker than the page on the left and the File List lighter on the right, the List under its title with a Sort pill, rows 68 pt tall carrying a name, a date and two lines of excerpt in one grey, a 3 pt accent bar on the open Document's row and no fill, and the Filter field at the foot. At search `sea` stands in the field, the list holds the name match and the content matches, and the pill reads Sort by Search Relevance. iA marks nothing a query matched, where Quill sets the matched word bold in a content match's excerpt, in the excerpt's own grey: that bold is Quill's own choice and not a gap. Five differences are decisions already taken and not gaps. The Organizer's sections are Quill's three — Locations, Pinned and Recents — where iA's are four, and the Location's name differs (the fixture's folder, `library`, against iA's iCloud). The date column reads the fixture's stamped dates on ours and the Mac copy's own dates on theirs, so its words and its width differ by what the dates are: the fixture's are last year's and read `Mar 14, 25`, the Mac copy's were written that morning and read a time — a shorter or longer date is the calendar and not a gap, and so is a name iA shortens in the middle beside a date of its own. The Mac copy's Library holds four more documents than the fixture, so the rows below the fixture's last are not a gap either. A row shows the name without its extension (`library.show_extensions` is false by default). The pane's type is Adwaita Sans, the GNOME UI face, where iA sets it in SF Pro Text, so a run of text a few pixels wider or narrower on one side is the two faces; the grounds, the greys, the sizes and the spacing are what to compare. And the Mac crop keeps that window's rounded corner, its traffic lights and the back and forward buttons over its List, which Quill's window does not draw. Where the page opens is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Page top rests the editor's own page top on a constant 30 logical px, measured off the Design oracle — the 164 device px its first line box stands below the window's top edge, less the 104 px its title bar takes — where the Parity oracle opens two pitches down, 72 px at the default step. So a side whose first line sits higher up the window is a decision already taken and not a gap

pieces.title: Live rendering
pieces.what: Markup folded away in place, headings on the ladder, furniture in the marker cells
pieces.judge: the page with Live on: whether the markup reads as a rendered page while it is still the source — the markers gone from every block but the one the caret is in, that block showing its source to edit, the headings larger by level, and the words landing on the same body column folded or not. The one state is asserted rather than paired (ADR 0017): neither oracle holds it, so tools/assert-state.mjs measures it off ours own pixels and the Piece takes that answer.

pieces.title: Preview
pieces.what: The rendered page beside the Editor, and in place of it
pieces.judge: nothing, and no critic is spent here: every state of this Piece names `assert`, so it is measured off ours' own pixels by tools/assert-state.mjs and shown to nobody (ADR 0017). Neither oracle holds the Preview — dev/legacy/ shows Markdown as source and has no rendered page at all, and iA Writer for Mac's own preview is that app's design rather than this one's, which is why #263 puts Preview outside ADR 0015's reach — so the states are won on arithmetic instead: in Split, the divider at half the window with the Editor's paper one side of it and the Template's the other, and the heading at the top of the rendered page centred in the pane it is drawn in; in Full, one paper across the whole window and that heading centred in the window itself. What a still cannot hold — the refresh, the scroll sync, a link opening — is the feature's Hand test.

pieces.title: Export
pieces.what: The Export dialog over the page, and the file it writes
pieces.judge: nothing, and no critic is spent here either: the one state names `assert`, so it is measured off ours' own pixels by tools/assert-state.mjs and shown to nobody (ADR 0017). Neither oracle holds an Export dialog — dev/legacy/ has none at all, and iA Writer for Mac's own is that app's dialog rather than this one's — so the state is won on arithmetic instead: the dialog standing over the page as a second ground, inside the window and centred on it, its Options expander open, and the file name seeded from the Document's own name. What a still cannot hold — the file that is written, the printer, the notification and the clipboard — is the feature's Hand test.

pieces.title: Settings
pieces.what: The Settings window over the page, a sidebar of five panes beside the pane it has selected
pieces.judge: nothing, and no critic is spent here: every state names `assert`, so it is measured off ours' own pixels by tools/assert-state.mjs and shown to nobody (ADR 0017). Neither oracle holds the window — dev/legacy/ has the grid the spec left behind, and iA Writer for Mac's own settings are that app's design rather than this one's — so the states are won on arithmetic instead: the window standing over the page on the pane the state opened, the sidebar's row for that pane the one drawn on a fill, and the pane's group heads and control rows counted. What a still cannot hold — what each row says, the writes to settings.toml, the search and the Palette's rows — is the feature's Hand test.

pieces.title: Syntax highlight
pieces.what: English words coloured by Category, with Focus and Live precedence
pieces.judge: the five Category colours and which words carry them: is the noun red the oracle's red and the verb blue its blue, and does the same word take the same colour on both sides. Three states are crops of the Design oracle at dev/ref/ia/mac-native/passage-syntax.md — all five Categories on each ground, and all five under Focus Sentence — so what is in front of you is the page itself and none of the furniture around it. The colours are docs/design.md row Syntax colours, measured off iA Writer for Mac on both grounds, so a Category reading a different hue or a different depth of colour on one side is a gap. So is a word split differently: docs/design.md row What a contraction colours puts `ca` and `n't` in different colours, `well` and `known` in different colours with the hyphen between them plain, and a possessive `'s` plain after its noun while the `'s` of `it's` is a verb — a side that paints a whole hyphenated compound one colour, or leaves an `n't` in the body's ink, is showing that row broken. At focus-sentence the dimmed rows carry no Category colour at all, one grey (docs/design.md row Dim over a Category), so a dimmed row holding a faint red is a gap and a dimmed row holding one flat grey is the row working. Four things are decisions already taken and not gaps. **Which Category a word is given**: that is the shipped tagger's answer and not this app's design. #310 § Out of Scope puts retraining or fine-tuning the tagger outside this work, and § Accuracy acceptance bounds it instead with a test — quill-engine/tests/syntax_accuracy.rs scores the shipped model against iA's own stills word by word and fails the build under 86 %; it stands at 89.3 %. So a word one side calls a noun and the other a verb, or colours where the other leaves it plain, is that bound and not a gap, however plainly wrong it looks: the two apps run different taggers on purpose. What is a gap is a colour, a dim or a split that differs — the things the rows above decide. The typeface: the Design oracle is set in Mono throughout (dev/ref/ia/mac-native/NOTES.md § The rig, which fits a cell grid Duo cannot), and ours is Duo, the port's default and the type Piece's own row — so glyph shapes, letter advances, cap heights and a line pitch one pixel apart are the two faces and the type ladder (docs/design.md rows Text sizes and Line pitch), not a gap. The caret: at focus-sentence both sides stand one after `more`, and what it is made of is the caret Piece's rows — Caret column, Caret width and Accent, which rests it at #00bfff on both grounds — so a bar that is a different blue, a different width or a different height is a decision already taken. The two all-Category states carry no bar on either side, which is the capture, not a caret that failed to draw. And where the page opens: docs/design.md row Page top rests the editor's own page top on a constant 30 logical px, so air above the first line that differs between two crops is the framing. The other two states are asserted under ADR 0017 and no critic is spent on them: no mac-native frame holds two Categories together and none holds Live at all, so adjectives-adverbs and live are measured off ours' own pixels. tools/assert-state.mjs measures expected and absent Role ink, preserved glyph coverage, colour inside the bright sentence rows, and colour on the scaled Live heading. Settings persistence and typing remain the feature Hand test.

pieces.title: Style check
pieces.what: Fillers, redundancies and clichés struck through on the prose stream
pieces.judge: a mac-native crop of the capture that measured this mark, one per state (#354, ADR 0015). dev/legacy/ has no Style check at all, so the Parity oracle holds none of these states and never will; what the nine are judged against is iA Writer itself, shot striking `dev/ref/style.md` on both grounds — every List on, Fillers alone, under Focus Sentence, under Syntax highlight with every Category, and with `Against all odds` held — which is the same passage the engine's fixture test and the capture's own states use, so the three cannot drift. Each crop is one row of that passage: the first body row for the seven states whose subject is the mark itself, because ours wraps a word earlier than the oracle does (our cell advances 26.0 device px against its 25.6) and that row is the longest stretch the two frames carry word for word; the selection's own row for the two `select` states. The two `docs/design.md` rows say what is ours and what is the oracle's. The rule's own geometry is a Face metric rather than a tag property — a `GtkTextTag` sets neither thickness nor position — so `tools/fontbuild.py` pins the oracle's 2 px on the x-height centre into the six Faces, which round 2 was lost on: ours ruled 4 px sitting 2 px high, and every critic said so. Which phrase belongs to which List the pixels cannot say, because all three Lists draw the same mark by design (#356 § The mark); that is held by quill-engine/tests/style_fixture.rs, which names every phrase of the passage by byte range and List. The toggles, the Settings rows, typing and persistence are the feature's Hand test. A GtkTextView draws selected glyphs in the selection node's colour, which overrides the tag under them, so the Editor covers a selected struck run with the paper and the fill and lays it out again in the mark's tier (#375); round 3 lost select-dark on the body ink that came back before it did.

pieces.title: Spell check
pieces.what: Misspelled prose words marked with the Design oracle’s own dots, withheld while the caret is still in the word
pieces.judge: a mac-native crop of the capture that measured this mark for eight of the ten states (#400, ADR 0015), and ours’ own pixels for the other two. dev/legacy/ had spell check off and its mark when on was the browser’s own, so the Parity oracle holds none of these states and never will; what the eight are judged against is iA Writer itself, shot over `dev/ref/spell.md` on both grounds — at rest, under Focus Sentence with the caret in the second sentence, under Syntax highlight with every Category, and with `recieved the notes` held — which is the same passage the engine’s fixture test uses, so the two cannot drift. Each crop is the passage’s first two body rows, which carry four of the seven marks and the one word that is not marked; ours wraps them word for word, at its own cell advance of 26.0 device px against the oracle’s 25.6. The mark is **a row of round dots and not a wave**: 6 device px across, an 8 px period, starting 12 px under the baseline at the capture’s 42.67 px em, in `#ed766b` light and `#cf807e` dark — two measured values, not one with an alpha. No Pango underline is that shape (its seven values are a wave or a rule, each at the face’s own thickness and position), so the Editor draws the dots itself from a property-free tag, at those sizes as shares of the em. **The mark does not dim**: out of focus the word falls to the dim tier and the dots hold their ink, which is the opposite of the Style check mark and is `docs/design.md` row *Spell mark under Focus, Syntax and a selection*. Seven words of the passage are marked and not eight: an all-caps word the dictionary does not hold (`DRAFFT`) is left alone, as a token carrying a digit (`2b`, `Q3`) is. Which words are misspelled the pixels cannot say; that is quill-engine/tests/spell_checker.rs, which names the seven over the fixture dictionary under dev/ref/spell/ every launch reads. The two states the capture shot no frame of — the caret parked at the end of `comittee`, where the word keeps its mark because the caret rule withholds only a word being typed, and the “no dictionary” state pinned by `--spell on:xx_XX` with the Library showing — are measured off ours’ own pixels by the `spell` assertion (ADR 0017): each is shot twice, the second `--spell off`, and the difference is read as seven marks under their lines of prose in the `spell` Role, or as no mark and one band of changed pixels, the status line. The typing case is `tools/gate keys spell`. The corrections menu, the toggles, the Settings rows and persistence are the spec’s Hand test. **What is judged here is the mark**: its two inks, its 8 px pitch, its six rows, the shape of one dot, where it sits under the baseline, which words wear it, and what it does under Focus, under Syntax highlight and over a selection. Three things in the same crop are not this Piece’s and no round turns on them. **The type’s advance and its line breaks are the page Piece’s**: ours sets 26.0 device px to the cell against the capture’s 25.6, because a judged shot hints its font metrics, so the same two rows come out 1664 px wide against 1638 and a mark spans its word about 1.6 % shorter than the glyphs do. The Design oracle’s own State 11 holds that ladder and #420 judged it ours. **Which words carry a Category colour is the `syntax` Piece’s**: our tagger leaves a word it does not hold uncoloured, so a misspelled word can read as a function word beside the oracle’s noun orange. The dots under it are what this Piece is asked about. **The selection composite is the design row’s**: `docs/design.md` row *Spell mark under Focus, Syntax and a selection* puts the fill under the mark and reads it at `#e2726b` over the light fill and `#cd8486` over the dark, which is what ours draws.

log.msg: Harness up: headless Chromium screenshots, latency bench, blind A/B pairing. Core editor engine written (textarea + mirror, incremental line render, custom caret, focus/typewriter, markdown tokenizer).

Reference package in: 49 real iA Writer screenshots (App Store, MS Store, ia.net) with verbatim transcriptions, Duo/Quattro/Mono fonts (OFL) with parsed metrics, measured spec sheet (paper #f9f9f9 / #1a1a1a, ink #1c1c1c / #cccccc, caret #00b5ff ≈0.15 em wide, line pitch ≈1.7×, 64-char measure, hanging # markers), latency bar from third-party measurements.

All nine pieces picked blind. Latency won on round 4: app-internal 2.43 ms mean / 15.61 ms worst (bar ≤5/≤16), real keys via /dev/uinput → presented frame 12.17 ms, caret settles 8.1 ms after the key (was 57 ms), cold launch to first document frame 370 ms. Final integration smoke passed in all three fonts and both themes.
